In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIV co-infection is associated with a more severe form of HCV-related liver diseases, with more severe liver histology and a more rapid progression to liver-related complications.
HCV infection is the most common cause of chronic liver disease in HIV-infected patients.
HIV infection is not a risk factor for the development of HCV-related liver complications but HIV infection is an aggravating factor for the severity of the HCV-induced liver disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impact of HIV co-infection on HCV infection is not only to increase the severity and the progression of liver disease but also to increase the rate of liver-related mortality.
